evidence.claim: AI accelerator substrates are described as becoming more complex across generations, with more layers, larger body size, finer features, and embedded components for power delivery; this supports the broader view that packaging and interconnect complexity can create chokepoints below the visible chip layer.
evidence.source_title: Ibiden: The Hidden Bottleneck Beneath AI

evidence.claim: The same source describes ABF film allocation and customer-funded substrate capacity as evidence that advanced substrate capacity can be strategically scarce and hard to substitute.
evidence.source_title: Ibiden: The Hidden Bottleneck Beneath AI

evidence.claim: The Spruce Pine high-purity quartz chain is described as operationally important to semiconductors, with raw quartz feeding crucible manufacturers and then silicon wafer manufacturers; qualification of new quartz sources can take years, sometimes up to a decade.
evidence.source_title: Underneath Every Chip — The Spruce Pine Problem

evidence.claim: Sakai Chemical is described as an upstream AI server MLCC dielectric-powder supplier, with electronic-materials demand linked by the author to AI server high-end MLCC mix; this supports the Serenity pattern of looking one step upstream from obvious AI hardware beneficiaries.
evidence.source_title: Sakai Chemical: The Upstream Play to AI Server MLCCs

evidence.claim: The same upstream-chokepoint logic can be applied to AI optical interconnects: if module-level demand is visible at AAOI, COHR and LITE, the less visible bottlenecks may sit in InP substrates, laser manufacturing equipment, high-speed drivers, optical manufacturing, and test capacity.
evidence.source_title: Cached Serenity Layer 2A supply-chain map and Layer 1 candidate universe

evidence.claim: AXTI is mapped as an underfollowed upstream InP substrate candidate because its exposure is one layer above visible AI optical modules; however, the provided evidence set does not yet prove AI datacenter customer concentration.

VECO is mapped as a second-order equipment candidate for InP laser and optical-component manufacturing capacity; provided evidence supports the node logic but still requires company-level order and customer verification.
AAOI is used as a reference demand anchor for AI optical modules because module-level ramps can validate or falsify upstream substrate, laser, component and manufacturing bottleneck hypotheses.

COHR is used as an integrated optical-stack reference anchor because its 800G/1.6T architecture choices may indicate whether InP substrates remain a bottleneck or are partly bypassed by alternative approaches.
LITE is used as a downstream optical-component reference anchor to interpret the technology mix of AI datacenter optical connectivity and its implications for upstream InP substrate intensity.

memory_update.text: AXTI should be tracked as the primary underfollowed upstream InP substrate candidate for AI optical interconnects, but survival to later layers requires proof that InP revenue/backlog is AI datacenter-driven rather than telecom or inventory-cycle driven.
VECO should be tracked as a second-order InP laser/compound-semiconductor equipment candidate; key validation is whether orders convert to 2026-2027 revenue and whether follow-on orders persist.

AAOI, COHR and LITE are not the underfollowed alpha lane but should remain reference anchors because their product ramps and architecture choices validate or falsify upstream substrate, laser and optical-component bottlenecks.
MTSI maps to the high-speed driver/component layer for 1.6T/3.2T optics; it may be underappreciated due to RF/analog classification, but needs production-socket and margin evidence.
FN maps to precision optical manufacturing, packaging and test capacity; the AI-specific relationship is plausible but needs separation of datacom AI programs from telecom recovery.
Need primary-source filings and earnings transcripts for AXTI, VECO, AAOI, COHR, MTSI, FN, AEIS, JCI, MTRN, LITE and KLAC before assigning durable company-level evidence scores.

Need current market caps, analyst coverage counts, and valuation/pricing checks to confirm which candidates still fit the underfollowed small/mid-cap discovery lane and which are already consensus AI infrastructure trades.
Need customer/supplier dependency mapping across InP substrates, EML lasers, DSPs, optical drivers, contract manufacturing, optical test, and hyperscaler/module customer ramps.

For second-order infrastructure names AEIS, JCI and MTRN, need evidence that AI-related demand is visible in backlog, revenue mix, margins or customer commentary rather than broad industrial, HVAC or semiconductor-cycle recovery.

summary: Candidate chunk maps AI optical-interconnect demand into a two-lane ticker relationship graph. Reference anchors AAOI, COHR, LITE and partially KLA validate end-demand, technology architecture, and inspection intensity, while the underfollowed lane centers on AXTI as upstream InP substrate exposure, VECO as InP laser/compound-semiconductor capacity equipment, MTSI as high-speed optical driver/component exposure, FN as precision optical manufacturing/test capacity, and second-order infrastructure/materials names AEIS, JCI and MTRN. Strongest relationship hypotheses are AXTI -> InP substrate bottleneck and VECO -> InP laser capacity expansion. Most claims still require primary-source verification from filings, earnings calls, order/backlog disclosures, customer announcements, and current market-cap/coverage checks.
